correctness.rationale: On a rooted fork the only proper order comparisons are o<=a for each leaf a. Universal FC means each root-arrow oRb to a leaf must repeat in every leaf row, while a root loop requires every leaf row nonempty. Universal BC means a leaf-to-root arrow forces that leaf row to contain all leaves, and a root loop requires the union of root/leaf leaf-successors to cover the leaves. Splitting by root loop e and root outgoing leaf set J gives exact F_k and I_k inclusion-exclusion formulas. For k large, zero-J cases give F_k=2*2^(k(k+1))(1+O(k2^-k)), I_k=2*2^(k*k)(1+O(k2^-k)), while j>=1 is negligible, proving 2^k I_k/F_k -> 1. Independently checked all 2^((k+1)^2) arbitrary labelled relations for k=1,2,3 against quantified FC and BC, obtaining (11,9),(185,81),(10943,2043), precisely the formulas; k=6,10,14 normalized ratios tend 1.

originality.rationale: FC and BC are foundational FIK/IK semantic conditions and not new. Published exact FIK and KI relation censuses for finite CHAINS concern totally ordered worlds rather than forks with incomparable leaves; their row monotonicity reduces differently. The present exact normal form and asymptotic exponential ratio for unrestricted labelled fork frames were not found as a corollary of the general logical axioms or chain counting formulas.
residual_risks: Other bi-relational logics may encode these same fork conditions under alternative FS/IK terminology; exhaustive priority unproved.
Reflexive/transitive frames, unlabeled isomorphism counts and taller posets are not claimed.
